summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for autologous stem cell transplant as treatment for multiple myeloma. He received melphalan conditioning chemotherapy and stem cell reinfusion on day zero. His hospital course was complicated by neutropenic fever, mucositis, and esophagitis. He developed fevers on multiple occasions, prompting broad-spectrum antibiotics and antifungal therapy, though no pathogen was isolated. Imaging revealed esophagitis and chronic left hydronephrosis, managed conservatively. He had asymptomatic VRE colonization in the urine, deemed non-treatment requiring. His pain was managed with opioids, adjusted during an episode of somnolence. He gradually recovered, became afebrile, and regained oral intake. He was discharged home in stable condition on oral medications including acyclovir, pantoprazole, magnesium, and pain control, with follow-up plans for urology, dermatology, and oncology.
